questions.question: In a young adult with new-onset diabetes, which clinical features in this case most strongly suggest MODY rather than type 1 or typical type 2 diabetes?
How do negative islet autoantibodies and a stimulated C-peptide of 0.83 nmol/L after glucagon help refine the differential diagnosis in this patient?
What is the pathophysiologic role of HNF1A in pancreatic beta-cell function, and how do HNF1A mutations lead to progressive hyperglycaemia?
Why can glycosuria occur early and disproportionately in HNF1A-MODY, even before severe fasting hyperglycaemia develops?
What are the major clues in the pedigree that support autosomal dominant inheritance, and why is this pattern important when evaluating early-onset diabetes?
When a patient with early-onset diabetes has a BMI in the overweight range and hypertriglyceridaemia, why should MODY still remain in the differential diagnosis?
After genetic confirmation of HNF1A-MODY, what treatment changes become reasonable, and why are low-dose sulfonylureas and GLP-1 receptor agonists particularly relevant options?
Why might SGLT2 inhibitors be relatively unfavorable in patients with HNF1A-MODY, despite their common use in other forms of diabetes?
How can a novel HNF1A variant be classified as pathogenic or likely pathogenic even if it is absent from ClinVar, and what types of evidence from this case support that interpretation?
